findings.title: Gate 10 (overlay-pixels) is vacuous: mutation-proven unable to fail on the never-draws wiring regression it was built to catch — the W5+F6/N15 fold is not real
findings.evidence: Mutation test (isolated copy, draw_noc_overlay removed from overlay_pixels_check): 'overlay-pixels: OK — the NOC panel paints (775 dark samples...)' — 775 >= 500 passes with the overlay NEVER DRAWN; healthy build: 5193. Compounding: the verb skips the flip+swizzle every other readback applies (overlay.odin:106-107), so it samples the vertically-mirrored band (y 24-624 vs the panel's 96-696) — region math unproven even in the healthy path
findings.detail: r3 F6 (W5 wiring gap, warned twice) was 'fixed' by this gate; the commit says it guards 'a wiring regression that never draws'. Mechanically proven it cannot: background map/forecast pixels alone clear the threshold. A claimed-fixed finding that is not fixed is a new blocker (round doctrine, r3 N11 precedent).
findings.recommended_fix: Baseline-relative check: render the frame twice (overlay on/off) and assert the DIFF inside the panel rect exceeds a floor (or assert row/text-band pixels specifically); apply the flip+swizzle normalization; verify by re-running this mutation.

findings.title: Readable-but-undecodable fallback (or merge alloc failure) still silently ships a ⚠-less atlas — the 'never a silent warning-less atlas' claim is overbroad
findings.evidence: fg := rl.LoadFontData(...); if fg == nil || ng == 0 { return glyphs, count } — same for merged == nil at :1421; only the os.read_entire_file ferr path (fixed this round) returns nil,0
findings.detail: Commit claims 'an unreadable FALLBACK with missing codepoints now FAILS the load (never a silent warning-less atlas)'. A truncated/corrupt TTF that reads but fails to rasterize returns ok — the negative control pins only the missing-FILE case.
findings.recommended_fix: Return nil,0 on fg==nil||ng==0 and merged==nil (mirror the ferr path); extend the negative control with a corrupt-bytes fixture.

findings.title: PP_SW_AUDIO seam branch (16 stub procs) is compiled by NO automated gate — signature drift stays green until a manual gallery build

findings.title: font_test pins leak raylib-owned memory: the guard test discards its atlas+recs ('_, _, ok :='), the mono/tabular tests unload the atlas image but not recs/glyphs

findings.detail: Test-process lifetime absorbs it; r3's probe fix (MemFree(glyphs)) was real but the sibling tests still leak.

findings.title: overlay_pixels_check never frees the LoadImageColors buffer

findings.title: font_merge_fallback's fail-loud nil-return paths leak the main glyph set they loaded

findings.detail: Callers os.exit(2) on nil (process death hides it); the negative-control test path returns and leaks per run.

findings.title: FONT_GLYPH_PADDING=4 is commented 'raylib's LoadFontEx default'; raylib sets glyphPadding=0 for loaded fonts
findings.evidence: rtext.c: 'font.glyphPadding = 0' (LoadFontFromMemory) + GenImageFontAtlas(..., font.glyphPadding, 0); comment claims the 4px padding is the LoadFontEx pattern
findings.detail: The 4px choice is a fine quality decision — it just is not raylib's default (blind said 2; the source says 0). Misattribution teaches the wrong invariant.
findings.recommended_fix: Reword: '4px padding (tighter than raylib's 0 — crisper glyph separation at small sizes)'.

findings.title: Health chips draw at 15px with a 15px row step — zero leading between stacked chips

findings.detail: Mechanical arithmetic (size == step); aesthetic verdict deferred to k3 per the vision caveat, but the zero-leading fact stands.
findings.recommended_fix: Step 17-18px for the 15px chips (or size 14 with step 15).

findings.title: build_probe_set re-implements the exported rnd.font_codepoints() instead of calling it

findings.recommended_fix: Call rnd.font_codepoints() in the harness probe.
